title: Adaptive flow-smoothing batch planner with KV spillover protection and soft-GPU quota
creator: Nora Patel
description: Problem: For streaming chat workloads we observe variable turn lengths and bursty arrivals that cause frequent KV cache pressure and transient OOMs on smaller GPU slabs. Current continuous batcher groups by arrival windows and priority tags but does not proactively protect KV slot allocation during sudden stream spikes. Goals: (1) Reduce p95/p99 latency regressions caused by KV eviction and GPU slab spilling during bursts, (2) Maintain throughput and token-cost efficiency by allowing small amounts of controlled spillover rather than hard-rejecting requests, (3) Provide predictable tail-latency SLOs for streaming chat while avoiding large memory overcommit. High-level idea: implement an Adaptive Flow-Smoother that: (a) computes an in-flight memory budget per GPU slab (soft-GPU quota) factoring current KV occupancy, predicted near-term token load, and configured latency SLO; (b) creates micro-batches by smoothing request arrivals into short smoothing windows but allows opportunistic bundling across adjacent windows when KV pressure is low; (c) when predicted KV delta exceeds slab budget, trigger a KV spillover protection policy that prefers lightweight partial-completions (early-token flushing) or re-route to lower-memory model variants as fallback. This should be compatible with streaming (incremental token emission) and preserve prefix/KV cache reuse where possible.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New planner runs in the runtime path behind a feature flag and does not regress median latency by >5% on synthetic baseline.
2) On bursty workload test, KV-triggered evictions reduced by >=60% compared to baseline.
3) p99 tail latency improves by at least 15% on the internal streaming-chat benchmark (same prompt mix used in performance lab).
4) No new OOM incidents in the stress test (10M tokens/day simulated) for the tested slab sizes (A100 40GB equivalent).
5) Console exposes a breakdown: smoothing-window-size, predicted KV delta, soft-quota utilization, and fallback counts.
6) Design doc and PR reviewed by runtime and infra leads and merged behind flag.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize predictive KV delta model (LR baseline + simple exponential smoothing of recent token arrival rates). — 2 days
Runtime: add soft-GPU quota metadata to slab allocator and expose an API for planner to reserve ephemeral KV slots. — 3 days
Batcher: implement flow-smoothing window with two tunable parameters: base_window_ms and opportunistic_merge_threshold. — 4 days
Policies: implement KV spillover protection handlers: early-token-flush, variant-reroute, and graceful-decline; add heuristics to prefer early flush for long-running streams. — 3 days
Observability: add metrics, tracing tags, and a Console panel prototype for the feature. — 2 days
Testing: unit tests, integration tests with synthetic bursty trace, and closed beta on dedicated cluster. — 4 days
Rollout: feature-flag, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error rate/latency thresholds. — 3 days
notes: We want to avoid increasing token-cost significantly; opportunistic merging should bias toward latency-sensitive traffic. Consider exposing user-configurable SLO weight (latency vs cost) at route level. The predictive model must be cheap — keep it as a moving-average + linear correction; evaluate whether a lightweight ML model is warranted later.

review_feedback: Infra Lead (Priya Rao): Ensure soft-quota reservations are best-effort and cannot deadlock; use try-reserve semantics with immediate fallback path.
Runtime Lead (Marco D'Souza): Avoid blocking on allocator calls in the hot path; use prefetch reservations computed off the critical path where possible.
SRE (Liam O'Connor): Add alert thresholds: fallback-reroute-rate > 1% for 5m should trigger auto-roll back and paging.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Predictive model underestimates immediate bursts -> still OOM. Mitigation: conservative safety margin in soft-quota and immediate fallback to variant-reroute when margin breached.
Risk: Added complexity increases median latency for smallest-turn requests. Mitigation: adaptive bypass for tiny-turn routes (per-route config) and tuning opportunistic_merge_threshold.
Risk: Multi-tenant contention for soft-quota leads to noisy neighbor problems. Mitigation: per-tenant share and global backpressure signal, plus documented operator knobs.
